item.text: {"piece_id":"03","title":"What to Watch After AI Enters the CAD Workflow","question":"What do these developments imply for the audience, and what should they watch next?","argument":"The near-term opportunity is not autonomous release-ready design, but faster creation, retrieval, and simulation preparation inside engineering workflows that retain explicit verification gates. Teams should watch whether vendors publish task-specific evidence that generated geometry, parametric features, and simulation-ready assets survive the checks that matter downstream: tolerances, manufacturability, boundary conditions, and physical transfer. The strongest adoption signal will be reproducible results on the team's own representative parts and processes, not broader agentic claims.","synthesis":"The evidence points to a practical division of labor: frontier models can accelerate drafts and interface work, while engineering teams must preserve native artifacts and independently test the properties the generation workflow did not check. MIT’s review distinguishes editable CAD output from tolerance and manufacturability validation; Engineering.com’s Backflip test shows that a mass check can verify a narrow property of two outputs while leaving feature reconstruction failures and shop-drawing generalization unresolved. Onshape and NVIDIA show vendors moving AI into parametric-feature authoring and CAD-to-simulation preparation, so the next decision is less whether to experiment than which release gates, logs, and representative test suites must remain outside the model’s authority.","limitations":"The available evidence is uneven: Backflip received a small curated editorial test, while the Onshape and NVIDIA workflow claims are vendor descriptions. No accepted source supplies a comparative, independently replicated evaluation of AI-generated features or simulation-ready assets against production tolerances, manufacturability, or physical transfer; teams should treat local pilots as necessary evidence rather than assume these workflows generalize.","claims":[{"claim_id":"03-c1","statement":"The MIT survey reports that frontier models
